newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Air, artillery attacks rain on Sri Lanka's north.
newsitem.headline: Air, artillery attacks rain on Sri Lanka's north.

text.p: The Sri Lankan military attacked Tamil Tiger targets from the air on Monday while ground troops consolidated in northern areas captured from the rebels after fierce fighting last week, the Defence Ministry said.
"Air and artillery fire was directed at given likely enemy targets in the area," a ministry statement said.
Artillery was being fired from the villages of Omanthai and Nedunkeni, which troops captured from the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) last week, a military spokesman told Reuters.
Troops on the offensive wrestled control of Omanthai, 14 km (nine miles) north of Vavuniya and northeastern Nedunkeni, about 40 km (25 miles) northeast of Vavuniya after fierce fighting.
"Troops continue to consolidate in the captured areas of Nedunkeni and north of Omanthai," the statement added.

Military officials in the area told Reuters that security forces were building bunkers and forward defence positions north and northeast of government-held Vavuniya, 220 km (135 miles) from the capital Colombo.

The multi-pronged offensive launched last week, codenamed "Jaya Sikuru", or "Sure of Victory", has managed to carve fresh inroads into the LTTE's northern Wanni heartland, a Defence Ministry official told Reuters.
"Troops have managed to capture and control land where no government soldier has stepped on for many years," he said.

The LTTE, fighting an ethnic war now in its 14th year for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in predominantly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east, control vast swathes of land in the mostly shrub-covered Wanni in the island's north.
Defence Ministry officials said two divisions were moving on separate flanks, trying to open a land supply route linking Vavuniya with the Jaffna peninsula, about 100 km (60 miles) further north.
Jaffna, the rebels' former stronghold and the capital of their would-be homeland, is under government control.
The rebels have accused the army of killing Tamil civilians and destroying property under the pretext of opening up a supply route.
"Tamil civilians are fleeing in their thousands, driven by warplanes and fighter helicopters that continue to fire on the civilian population," said the LTTE's international spokesman, Anton Raja.
"Night and day, artillery shells are being fired at civilian centres in the Wanni," he said by telephone from his London office.

According to figures released by the Defence Ministry, eight soldiers were killed in overnight fighting while 29 were wounded, bringing the official military death toll from the six-day old offensive to 67 and those wounded to 96.
Hospital sources said some 320 soldiers have been wounded.
The ministry said troops monitoring LTTE transmissions confirmed 181 dead, including several leaders and 316 wounded.
"However, terrorist casualties are very much higher than this according to ground troops," the statement said.
The LTTE have said they have lost only 37 fighters in the offensive.
Journalists have not yet been allowed in the battle zone.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14the year. The rebels say the toll is higher.
